article_blocks.text: Strain Type: Indica-dominant hybrid
Genetics: Moonfog × P. Face OG × High Octane
Breeder: Humboldt Seed Company
THC Content: 26%
CBD Content: N/A
Terpene Profile: N/A
Primary Flavors: Gas, earthy Kush, sweet floral notes, spice
Flowering Time (Indoor): 55–65 days
Outdoor Harvest Time: October 1 – 10
Indoor Yield: Very high potential
Outdoor Yield: Very high potential
Grow Difficulty: Intermediate

Moon Fog looks like the kind of weed its name promises: dark green and purple-flecked flowers buried under enough frost to give the buds an almost lunar appearance. Humboldt Seed Company built the cultivar around heavy resin, large production, and an immersive indica-oriented experience rather than a bright candy flavor or ultra-fast seven-week finish. Mature plants can carry chunky, heavily coated flowers whose appearance shifts noticeably as cooler conditions deepen the purple highlights. The visual appeal is matched by a pungent aromatic direction dominated by OG-style gas and earthy resin, with sweeter floral or berry nuances sometimes appearing beneath the heavier fuel.

The experience is more dynamic than the indica label initially suggests. Humboldt describes a “celestial” high and dreamy fog, language that reflects an early cerebral component before deeper relaxation becomes obvious. Creativity and euphoria can emerge during the beginning of a session, but the cultivar is equally capable of becoming physically heavy as the dose builds. A 55–65 day flowering window gives growers some phenotype-dependent variation, while an October 1–10 outdoor harvest keeps the strain within a practical early-autumn schedule. The combination of dramatic frost, high production potential, and a head-to-body progression gives Moon Fog a personality that feels distinctly different from either a straightforward OG Kush or a purely sedating indica.
Genetics and Lineage

Humboldt Seed Company publishes the parental formula as Moonfog × P. Face OG × High Octane. The breeder does not currently specify a more detailed grouping of those three components, so the lineage should be preserved exactly as stated rather than rearranged into an assumed two-stage pedigree. P. Face OG contributes much of the recognizable OG character, including pungent fuel, earthy resin, dense flower formation, and the heavier physical qualities associated with West Coast Kush-derived cannabis .

High Octane reinforces that side of the family rather than softening it. Genetics carrying the High Octane name are closely associated with gas, chemical sharpness, Kush earthiness, and potent relaxing effects, all of which fit the finished cultivar’s heavier aromatic and experiential direction. The Moonfog component provides the breeding foundation around which Humboldt built the commercial line, but the company does not publish deeper ancestry for that component on the current product page. Inventing additional parentage would therefore create false precision.

What matters more than speculative ancestry is the character Humboldt chose to preserve. The commercial population favors heavy trichome coverage, purple-flecked flowers, substantial yields, and a powerful cerebral-to-dreamy experience. Grower observations also indicate that some plants move beyond pure OG fuel into sweeter floral, berry, or creamy territory as the flowers mature. That variation makes sense in a seed line carrying several potent modern hybrid influences, while the strong gas-and-resin foundation keeps the overall identity recognizable.
Effects and Experience

The first stage can be surprisingly cerebral. Instead of immediately flattening the consumer into a chair, Moon Fog may open with a rush of euphoria, imaginative thinking, and greater interest in music, visual media, or creative activities. Familiar surroundings can seem more immersive, and thoughts may become less linear as the high develops. Humboldt’s cosmic description is dramatic, but it does capture the slightly detached, expansive character that stronger servings can produce.

Physical relaxation gradually becomes harder to ignore. Tension eases, movement feels less urgent, and the mentally elevated beginning can drift into the “fog” referenced in the name. At moderate amounts, the experience may remain enjoyable for an unstructured creative afternoon or relaxed social setting. Larger servings are more likely to reduce motivation and turn the session toward movies, music, food, or simply staying in one place.

The breeder does not attach a universal THC number to the current seed line, and that is preferable to assuming every plant has identical potency. Commercial descriptions often position Moon Fog as strong cannabis, and the effects warrant the same respect given to other high-potency OG-derived hybrids. Too much may produce anxiety, dizziness, short-term memory disruption, dry mouth, or excessive heaviness. Consumers unfamiliar with potent marijuana should approach a new batch conservatively until its strength becomes clear.
Medical Benefits

The transition from cerebral uplift into stronger physical calm may interest medical marijuana consumers who prefer an effect that develops gradually. Cannabis with similar subjective characteristics is sometimes chosen by individuals seeking temporary relief from physical discomfort, appetite changes, or difficulty settling down after daily activity. The early euphoric component may make the experience feel less immediately sedating than a traditional heavy indica, while the later stages can become considerably more relaxing.

Moon Fog itself has not been evaluated in controlled clinical trials as a treatment for chronic pain, anxiety, insomnia, depression, or another medical condition. Research involving cannabis and cannabinoids more generally supports potential benefits for certain forms of chronic pain and nausea, but those findings depend on formulation, dose, patient population, and route of administration. They cannot automatically be applied to a particular flower cultivar because its recreational effects sound relaxing.

Potency can also complicate therapeutic use. THC may increase anxiety, impair short-term memory, reduce coordination, or produce more sedation than intended, especially when doses are high. Cannabis can interact with certain medications as well. Medical use should therefore be guided by current cannabinoid testing, personal tolerance, and appropriate healthcare advice rather than assumptions based on an indica classification.
Flavor Profile and Aroma

Fuel forms the deepest part of Moon Fog’s aromatic identity. Mature flowers can carry the pungent hydrocarbon character associated with OG cannabis, backed by damp earth, resin, and dry spice. Breaking apart the buds tends to intensify the gas while releasing greener herbal notes from deeper inside the flower. The profile is darker and more traditional than the fruit-candy aromas common in many newer California hybrids.

Some expressions become more complex as they cure. Sweet floral tones may rise above the gas, and certain plants can show berry-like or creamy accents that soften the otherwise aggressive Kush character. Those lighter notes are not guaranteed across every seed plant, but they help explain why different Moon Fog phenotypes can smell noticeably different while still sharing the same resinous foundation.

Humboldt Seed Company does not publish a permanent compound-by-compound terpene profile for the current line. Assigning universal percentages of caryophyllene, limonene, myrcene, pinene, or another terpene would therefore be speculative. Batch-specific laboratory testing is the appropriate way to establish chemical composition. A slow dry and patient cure are especially worthwhile because the sweeter floral and berry tones can disappear quickly under excessive heat, leaving only the heavier earth and fuel.
Growing Information

Moon Fog is promoted first and foremost as a highly productive plant. Humboldt describes yield as exceptional, and grower observations support the idea that even lower branches can develop substantial flower mass when the plant receives adequate light. Vegetative growth may initially appear relatively upright or compact, but some plants stretch significantly after flowering begins. Indoor cultivators should therefore avoid assuming that the plant will remain short simply because it is classified as an indica.

Indoor flowering takes approximately 55–65 days. The range is wider than the fixed schedules Humboldt publishes for some of its other cannabis varieties , suggesting meaningful phenotype and environmental variation. Flowers build considerable density as maturity approaches and become heavily coated in frost. Purple flecking often develops through the buds, especially where cooler conditions encourage stronger pigment expression. Large tops may need support once the resinous flowers gain their final weight.

Because the cultivar can stretch more than expected, canopy planning is useful before the flowering transition. Topping, branch positioning, or trellising can help spread upright growth across available lighting and keep tall tops from crowding the ceiling. Dense flower production also makes interior airflow important. Removing excessive congestion from the lower canopy can improve circulation without stripping away productive branches unnecessarily.

Outdoor maturity generally arrives between October 1 and October 10. That relatively early window works well for many Northern Hemisphere gardens because it avoids the very late finishes associated with some Haze-influenced or tropical cultivars. Humboldt does not publish an exact outdoor yield weight, and production should not be reduced to one universal figure. Root volume, sunlight, soil quality, plant spacing, climate, and vegetative duration can change outdoor harvests dramatically.

Heavy trichome production deserves careful handling at harvest. Rough trimming, compression, or warm drying environments can damage the resin layer responsible for much of the strain’s appearance and potency. Dense flowers should dry slowly enough for internal moisture to escape without allowing the exterior to become brittle first. Once curing begins, the sharper OG gas settles slightly and the sweeter floral, berry, or creamy undertones become easier to distinguish.
FAQ
What are the genetics of Moon Fog?
Humboldt Seed Company lists Moon Fog as Moonfog × P. Face OG × High Octane. The breeder does not currently publish a more detailed grouping or deeper ancestry for the Moonfog component.
Is Moon Fog indica or sativa?
Humboldt classifies the cultivar as indica. Its experience still contains a noticeable cerebral and euphoric beginning before progressing toward a dreamier, more physically relaxing state.
What does Moon Fog taste like?
The profile generally emphasizes OG-style gas, earthy Kush, resin, and spice. Depending on phenotype, sweeter floral, berry, or creamy notes may appear beneath the heavier fuel character.
How long does Moon Fog take to flower?
Indoor plants generally require approximately 55–65 days of flowering. Outdoors, Humboldt lists an expected harvest period from roughly October 1 through October 10.
Is Moon Fog a high-yield strain?

Yes. Humboldt Seed Company specifically describes the cultivar as having exceptional yield potential. Exact indoor and outdoor weights vary according to plant size, environment, lighting, root space, and cultivation method.
Final Thoughts on Moon Fog

Moon Fog is built around the characteristics that made powerful West Coast indica hybrids so enduring: pungent fuel, dense resinous flowers, substantial production, and effects capable of becoming deeply relaxing. P. Face OG and High Octane reinforce the gassy foundation, while Humboldt’s Moonfog breeding material adds enough variation for sweeter floral and berry expressions to appear in selected plants.

The garden performance is equally important. A 55–65 day flowering period, early-October outdoor harvest, high production potential, and thick trichome coverage create a commercially attractive package. The main cultivation consideration is stretch, since some plants can rise considerably once bloom begins despite their indica classification. Giving the canopy room early is easier than correcting excessive height late.

For consumers, the progression from cerebral euphoria toward a hazier, more physically settled state defines the strain better than any simple indica label. Heavy frost and purple flecks supply the visual drama, while gas, earth, spice, and occasional sweetness provide the aromatic depth. Moon Fog ultimately lives up to the name through the experience itself: an elevated opening that gradually disappears into a much dreamier haze.
